instrument: Pediatric Language Assessment — developmental milestone check
source: Milestones sourced verbatim from ASHA Communication Milestones (asha.org/public/developmental-milestones). Examples authored by Cue in Indian English for familiarity. This is a structured developmental reference informing clinical judgment, not a standalone diagnostic tool.

age_bands.label: Birth to 12 months
age_bands.note: Pre-verbal band — almost entirely social communication and early sound play. Language and literacy sections are minimal by design; this is developmentally correct.

speech.milestone: Coos — makes sounds like ooooo, aahh, mmmmm
speech.example: Baby makes soft vowel sounds when content, lying down or being held

speech.milestone: Babbles long strings of sounds, like mamamama, bababa, upup
speech.example: Child repeats syllables in a string — 'ba-ba-ba', 'ma-ma-ma' — during play

speech.milestone: Makes sounds that differ depending on whether happy or upset
speech.example: You can tell from the sound alone whether the child is pleased or distressed

language.milestone: Alerts to sound
language.example: Child turns or stills when you clap or call from behind

language.milestone: Quiets or smiles when you talk
language.example: Child settles or smiles when amma speaks softly

language.milestone: Makes sounds back and forth with you
language.example: Child 'takes turns' — you make a sound, child answers with a sound

language.milestone: Points, waves, and shows or gives objects
language.example: Child gives you a toy, waves bye-bye, or points at the fan

literacy.milestone: Looks at pictures when you read
literacy.example: Child looks at a bright picture book while you name what's on the page

speech.milestone: Uses a lot of new sounds, so babbling sounds more like real speech
speech.example: Child's babble starts to have the rhythm and tune of a sentence

language.milestone: Follows directions — like 'Give me the ball', 'Come here', 'Show me your nose'
language.example: Child gives the ball when asked, or points to their nose on request

language.milestone: Uses first words
language.example: Child uses a few true words — 'amma', 'ball', 'no', 'more'

language.milestone: Points to ask a question or to show you something
language.example: Child points at the dog and looks at you to share it

literacy.milestone: Shows interest in books and pictures
literacy.example: Child brings you a book or turns pages to look at pictures

speech.milestone: Speech may not always be clear — like 'du' for shoe or 'dah' for dog
speech.example: Child's words are recognisable to family but sounds are still simplified

language.milestone: Uses and understands at least 50 different words for food, toys, animals, and body parts
language.example: Child names or points to roti, ball, dog, eyes, and many more on request

language.milestone: Puts two or more words together — like 'more water' or 'go outside'
language.example: Child combines words — 'more water', 'amma come', 'go out'

language.milestone: Follows two-step directions — like 'Get the spoon and put it on the table'
language.example: Child does both parts — 'pick up the ball and give it to me'

literacy.example: Child turns the pages one at a time while you read together

speech.milestone: Correctly produces p, b, m, h, w, d, and n in words
speech.example: Child says these sounds clearly in words like 'papa', 'ball', 'mango', 'hand'

speech.milestone: Correctly produces most vowels in words
speech.example: Vowel sounds in the child's words are clear and correct

speech.milestone: Speech is becoming clearer but may not be understandable to unfamiliar listeners
speech.example: Family understands the child, but a stranger may not catch everything

language.milestone: Uses word combinations often, but may occasionally repeat some words or phrases, like 'baby-baby-baby sit down' or 'I want-I want juice'
language.example: Child speaks mostly in phrases, with some normal repetition — 'I want-I want water'

language.milestone: Tries to get your attention by saying 'Look at me!'
language.example: Child calls out to make you watch — 'amma, see!'

language.milestone: Says their name when asked
language.example: Child tells you their name when you ask 'What is your name?'

language.milestone: Uses some plural words like 'birds' or 'toys'
language.example: Child adds -s for more than one — 'balls', 'dogs'

language.milestone: Uses -ing verbs like 'eating' or 'running'; adds -ed for past actions, like 'looked' or 'played'
language.example: Child says 'eating', 'running', and 'I played', 'amma went'

language.milestone: Gives reasons for things and events, like needing a coat when it's cold
language.example: Child explains — 'I want sweater because cold'

language.milestone: Asks 'why' and 'how'
language.example: Child asks 'why?' and 'how?' about everyday things

language.milestone: Answers questions like 'What do you do when you are sleepy?'
language.example: Child answers simple reasoning questions — 'What do you do when you are hungry?'

literacy.milestone: Understands that letters and pictures mean something
literacy.example: Child points at their name or a familiar picture and knows it 'says' something

speech.milestone: Correctly produces t, k, g, f, y, and -ing in words
Says all the syllables in a word
speech.example: Child says the whole word — 'banana', not 'nana'

speech.milestone: Says the sounds at the beginning, middle, and end of words
speech.example: Child produces first, middle, and last sounds — the 't' in 'cat', not just 'ca'

speech.milestone: By age 4, talks smoothly — does not repeat sounds, words, or phrases most of the time
speech.example: Child speaks in a smooth flow without frequent repeating or getting stuck

speech.milestone: By age 4, speaks so people can understand most of what they say (may still miss l, r, sh, ch, s, v, z, th)
speech.example: A stranger understands most of what the child says; later sounds may still be off

language.milestone: Compares things, with words like 'bigger' or 'shorter'
language.example: Child compares — 'this ball is bigger', 'my pencil is shorter'

language.milestone: Tells you a story from a book or a video
language.example: Child retells what happened in a story or a cartoon they watched

language.milestone: Understands and uses more location words, like 'inside', 'on', and 'under'
language.example: Child follows and uses 'put it inside the box', 'the cat is under the chair'

language.milestone: Uses words like 'a' or 'the' when talking, like 'a book' or 'the dog'
language.example: Child uses small connecting words — 'the dog', 'a ball' — in sentences

literacy.milestone: Pretends to read alone or with others
literacy.example: Child holds a book and 'reads' it aloud from memory or by looking at pictures

literacy.milestone: Recognizes signs and logos like STOP
literacy.example: Child recognises familiar signs and logos — a STOP sign, a known shop name

literacy.milestone: Pretends to write or spell and can write some letters
literacy.example: Child scribbles 'writing' and can form a few real letters

speech.milestone: Produces most consonants correctly, and speech is understandable in conversation
speech.example: The child is clear to most listeners in everyday conversation

speech.milestone: Blends word parts, like cup + cake = cupcake; identifies some rhyming words
speech.example: Child joins parts — 'foot + ball = football' — and spots rhymes like 'cat' and 'hat'

language.milestone: Produces grammatically correct sentences; sentences are longer and more complex
language.example: Child speaks in full, correct sentences that join ideas together

language.milestone: Tells stories with main characters, settings, and connecting words like 'and'
language.example: Child tells a story with who, where, and 'and then...' linking events

language.milestone: Uses at least one irregular plural form, like 'feet' or 'men'
language.example: Child uses irregular plurals — 'feet', not 'foots'

language.milestone: Understands and uses location words, like 'behind', 'beside', and 'between'
language.example: Child follows 'stand behind amma', 'sit between us'

language.milestone: Uses more words for time — like 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow' — correctly
language.example: Child uses time words correctly — 'we went yesterday', 'school is tomorrow'

language.milestone: Follows simple directions and rules to play games
language.example: Child follows the rules of a simple game like snakes-and-ladders or a turn-taking game

literacy.milestone: Recognizes and names 10 or more letters and can usually write their own name
literacy.example: Child names at least 10 letters and writes their own name

literacy.milestone: Locates the front of a book and its title
literacy.example: Child knows which way the book opens and points to the title

literacy.milestone: Imitates reading and writing from left to right
literacy.example: Child moves finger left-to-right while 'reading' and writing
